clarity.justification: The method is well aligned with the hypothesis: it scores tokens using "aggregated downstream attention" and "causal importance via activation ablation," then measures the resulting "accuracy vs. mean tokens generated" trade-off against explicit baselines. The prediction is directional and partly quantified—"30-50%" token reduction with "near-equal accuracy"—so failing to obtain that reduction provides a recognizable negative outcome, but "near-equal" has no numerical tolerance and neither "small subset" nor "frequently" versus "rarely" is thresholded. Important details also remain ambiguous, including which layers are mean-ablated, how offline causal scores define when "sufficient load-bearing content has accumulated," and how the controller forces an answer rather than merely truncating generation.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is training the probe "to predict, at generation time, whether sufficient load-bearing content has accumulated to answer correctly" and converting that prediction into the "skip filler" controller; this requires custom label construction and intervention logic, but it is implementable rather than an undefined magic operation. The named models—"Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Llama-3.1-8B"—and datasets "GSM8K, MATH" and "ProntoQA" exist, while attention extraction, residual-stream ablation, linear/MLP probes, and generation control are supported by standard transformer tooling. Resources are concretely named at three model and three benchmark settings, and the proposal supplies a "30-50%" target, but it gives no problem sample sizes, number of ablated tokens, layer coverage, or run counts. The negative branch is runnable because it includes full-CoT and early-exit controls, attention-only/causal-only ablations, and the explicit check that low-score versus high-score token ablations differ in answer-flip frequency, although the precise ablation protocol still needs specification.
